title: USDC as Gas on Your L1
summary: Bridge USDC in as your L1's native token
description: Makes USDC the gas token of an Avalanche L1. USDC locked on the C-Chain in an ICTT TokenHome is minted as the L1's native coin by a NativeTokenRemote through the Native Minter precompile, and burned again on the way back.
prompts: Use USDC as the gas token on my L1
My L1's users should pay fees in stablecoins
Bridge USDC from the C-Chain as the native coin of my chain

remote.description: Your L1, with the Native Minter precompile and ICM enabled

params.name: teleporterManager
params.description: May pause Teleporter versions on both contracts

params.name: nativeAssetSymbol
params.description: Symbol of the L1's native coin

params.name: initialReserveImbalance
params.description: Native coins that exist on the L1 before the bridge (from genesis), in 18-decimal base units. Must be above 0. Match the genesis allocation for full backing; the default treats genesis coins as unbacked, which suits testnet.

params.name: burnedFeesReportingRewardPercentage
params.description: Share of burned fees paid to whoever reports them back to the home, 0 to 100

params.name: amount
params.description: Test transfer in USDC base units (6 decimals); the default is 0.5 USDC

params.name: recipient
params.description: Receives native coins on the L1

params.name: requiredGasLimit
params.description: Gas for the remote to mint on delivery

prerequisites: An L1 with the Native Minter precompile, interoperability, and a relayer to the C-Chain: l1-quickstart with nativeMinter, interoperability and enableManagedRelayer
The builder is a Native Minter admin on the L1 (l1-quickstart seeds the owner address)
USDC on Fuji from the Circle faucet listed in the registry, which sends 1 USDC per request
Native gas on the L1 for the deployer, from the genesis allocation

contracts.name: NativeTokenRemote
contracts.description: Mints and burns the L1's native coin

contracts.name: ERC20
contracts.description: Standard ERC-20 ABI, for USDC approvals

steps.title: Make sure a relayer serves both chains
Deploy a USDC TokenHome on the C-Chain
Let the remote mint native coins
Register the remote with its home
Wait for the home to learn about the remote
Read how much USDC collateral the remote needs
Back the L1's pre-existing supply with USDC
Bridge USDC in as native gas
Wait for the native coins to be minted

checks.description: The remote is collateralized once the first transfer lands
Native coins were minted from bridged USDC

review: The L1's genesis enables contractNativeMinterConfig; without it the NativeTokenRemote constructor reverts.
initialReserveImbalance is above 0 and matches the genesis supply the builder wants backed; state plainly how much native supply is unbacked.
tokenHomeDecimals is USDC's 6 from the registry, while the native coin has 18; ICTT scales between them.
Only the NativeTokenRemote is enabled on the Native Minter; the admin role stays with the builder, not the deployer.
Collateral steps are skipped when collateralNeeded is 0, because addCollateral reverts in that case.

frontend.summary: Top up gas on the L1 with USDC, and turn it back into USDC later.
audience: Users who need gas on the L1 and hold USDC
journeys: Top up: 'Add 10 USDC of gas', with the USDC balance on the C-Chain and the gas balance on the L1 side by side.
Follow it to arrival, then the L1 gas balance updates.
Cash out: turn gas back into USDC on the C-Chain.
Explain in one line that gas on this L1 is paid in this USDC-backed coin, so users don't need AVAX there.
flows: Top up: approve TokenHome for the USDC amount, then send(input, amount) with the L1 as destination; show the native balance on the L1 updating after delivery.
Withdraw: on the L1 call send(input) on NativeTokenRemote with msg.value equal to the amount; USDC returns to the recipient on the C-Chain.
Show amounts as USDC on both sides: 1 USDC (1000000 base units) becomes 1 native coin (10^18 base units).
Explain that L1 gas fees are paid in this coin and burned; reportBurnedTxFees syncs burned fees back to the home.
